items.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: My co-host was Clifton Davis, before Lou Rawls got involved.

ctx.x: Let’s talk a little bit about some of the organizations whose work you’ve quietly supported. By quietly, I don’t mean secretly, because many of them appreciated you publicly by honoring you. I’ll name some of them. We can talk about any ones that you want. I’m thinking about the Urban League. I’m thinking about the NAACP, The Brotherhood Crusade, UNCF [United Negro College Fund].

Oh yes. I did the very first telethon. I was the hostess for the first UNCF telethon. My co-host was Clifton Davis, before Lou Rawls got involved. So that was a special thing for me. And having been on many of the black campuses, it’s just wonderful to support them. I’ve also discovered that – and it disturbs me – that 80% of black students in college are female. There’s a problem there. That’s not – where are my men? Where are my guys? That’s distressing. I found that out going to meetings. I find out stuff like…
What do you say to a young person who says, “Well, you didn’t finish school”?
